title: The Burning Oath Again
premise: When the valley's protective wards collapse and the stars vanish, Coral Zhou discovers her late mistress bound the valley not to hide from magic, but to imprison a fragment of the thing that wears King Aldric's crown. Dragged out by a disgraced oath-warden named Sef, Coral learns her own bloodline holds the counter-oath needed to unbind the king before the thirteenth moon turns and the crown-thing becomes permanent. Betrayed by the warden council who would rather kill Aldric than risk another binding, Coral chooses justice outside the law: she performs the unbinding herself, shattering the crown and taking its inherited burden into her own name. The stars return, but Coral ends the story changed — no longer an apprentice, but the keeper of a new, freely-given oath.
about_author: Wren Whitlock is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval oath-scrolls before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about inheritance, broken promises, and the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. On the eve of her final apprenticeship test, the valley wards fail and the sky goes black; her dying mistress presses a scorched oath-token into her hand and names a king Coral has never heard of. Riders from beyond the valley arrive hunting 'the keeper.' Emotional beat: terror and reluctant responsibility as Coral flees the only home she's known.

chapters.title: A Crown That Eats Its Wearer
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, with interludes from Sef. Guided by Sef through a starless countryside, Coral reaches the capital and sees King Aldric — half himself, half hollowed thing. She learns her bloodline wrote the original binding and that the thirteenth moon is nearly full. Emotional beat: grief curdling into resolve when she realizes her mistress sacrificed everything to buy time.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Alternating Coral and Sef POVs converge at the coronation-eve ritual. The warden council betrays them, choosing regicide over risk, and Sef takes a mortal wound holding the door while the crown-thing offers Coral power in exchange for walking away. Emotional beat: the climax — Coral refuses the bargain and speaks the counter-oath in her own name, unbinding the king as the moon completes its turn.

chapters.title: What the Oath Leaves Behind
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Aldric, freed but broken, abdicates rather than rule what he cannot remember being; the warden council fractures under exposure of their betrayal. Coral buries Sef beneath returning starlight and accepts the mantle of oath-keeper — not inherited this time, but chosen. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace and a new identity forged outside any law but her own.
